summary: Client abort pattern + inflight retries created cascading backpressure, causing elevated 5xx rates in us-east prod
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-12 10:05 UTC NimbusChat (dedicated tenant) observed a rapid rise in 5xx responses from our hosted API. Errors were concentrated on streaming chat and small-payload POST requests. Impact: degraded customer experience (unusable chat sessions) for ~30% of tenant traffic during the window; alerted via customer escalation. Initial observation suggests a pattern of frequent client aborts (TCP RST / HTTP client disconnects) combined with aggressive client-side hedged retries that kept requests inflight and amplified upstream backpressure.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) In a dedicated tenant routing in us-east, open several long-lived streaming sessions (chat) to simulate interactive clients.
2) Simulate flaky mobile network by sending client TCP RST for in-flight streaming requests at ~10-20% probability.
3) On abort, client SDK issues immediate hedged retry to a second route without exponential backoff.
4) Observe accept queue growth on api-gateway, then rising proxy 502/503 and serving-runtime OOM / eviction events under sustained load.
logs: 2026-03-12T10:07:12Z apigw[us-east] WARN accept_queue=1245 backlog_ms=3200 route=tenant/1234 - conn-reset-from-client
2026-03-12T10:07:13Z apigw[us-east] ERR proxy_upstream=502 upstream=serving-77 instance=srv-77 reason=upstream-eof
2026-03-12T10:07:14Z runtime[serving-77] ERR oom-kernel-signal process=llm-worker thread=main token_stream=aborted
investigation_notes: 10:15 - Support (Maya): validated tenant impact, collected request ids and sample headers from customer logs; escalated to SRE.
10:27 - SRE (Omar): confirmed apigw accept_queue growth correlated with client abort spike; observed many half-open streams and repeated immediate retries from client IP ranges.

10:40 - Hypothesis: hedged retries + client aborts cause acceptance queue saturation on apigw which propagates backpressure to serving-runtime. Serving-runtime then triggers eviction and OOM under high concurrency, producing 502/503.
11:02 - Observed evidence: runtime instance srv-77 showed repeated memory growth then eviction, aligned with tenant-prefetch locks and KV cache thrash over the same period.
11:20 - Short-term mitigation put in place: lower tenant concurrency cap and enabled per-tenant hedged-retry-suppressor for tenant 1234; results: 5xx dropped to ~3% within 10 minutes.
11:45 - Confirmed customer SDK version is using immediate hedged retry policy (v2.3.1). Requested customer to roll back to v2.2.0 which has linear retry backoff for streaming.
resolution_notes: Mitigation: Applied per-tenant rate-cap at api-gateway and enabled hedged-retry-suppressor. Reduced prefetch window for tenant to limit kvcache churn.
Workaround for customer: recommended temporary SDK config change to add a 200ms jitter and exponential backoff on retry, and to upgrade when patch is available.

Permanent fix (next steps): engineering to add server-side hedged-retry detection and suppressor at apigw, and enhance serving-runtime to fail fast on prefetch lock contention rather than queueing. See linked PR.
Follow-up items: SRE runbook update (add section for client-abort + retry patterns), coordinate with Customer Success to confirm SDK rollout, schedule a dedicated postmortem if SLA thresholds met.
